messages.subject: 3PL prior for the guessing parameters
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am trying to run a 3PL model with specified prior distributions. Specifically, prior of a1 ~ lognormal(0, 1), g (guessing) ~ beta(4, 16). However, mirt gave me warnings when I specified the prior of g to a beta distribution. Below is what I got. Also, the result only gave DIC; AIC and BIC were not given. Can I only use a normal distribution as the prior for the guessing parameters?

> Model_3PL = mirt.model('F1 = 1-40
+                           PRIOR = (1-40,a1,lnorm, 0, 1),(1-4,g,beta, 4, 16)')

>   Result_3PL = mirt(Data, Model_3PL, itemtype = "3PL")
Iteration: 76, Log-Lik: -11836.391, Max-Change: 0.00008Warning messages:
1: Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior 
2: Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior 
3: Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior 
4: Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior 

Thanks,
June
